The New BMW 3 Series Is Stretched So Much That It Is Almost a 5 Series in China
8 photos
Photo: Ministry of Industry and Information Technology China
The long-wheelbase BMW 3 Series built specifically in China for China has significantly grown in size, reaching a wheelbase nearly as long as that of the American-spec 5 Series. It is all in the name of comfort and space for customers who prefer to ride in the back seat and be chauffeured.
Filings with China’s Ministry of Industry and Information Technology (MIIT) reveal that the stretched BMW 3 Series is larger than ever before. While the standard 3 Series remains a compact sports sedan, the Chinese variant, produced by the BMW Brilliance Joint Venture, pushes directly into midsize territory.
The U.S.-spec 5 Series sits on a wheelbase measuring 117.9 inches (2,995 millimeters), while the China-spec 3 Series comes with a wheelbase stretched to 116.9 inches (2,970 millimeters) instead of the standard Western 112.6 inches (2,860 millimeters).
The long-wheelbase 3 Series is 191.5 inches (4,865 millimeters) long in China , inching closer to the length of the American 5 Series, which is 199.2 inches (5,060 millimeters) long. The standard 3 Series measures 187.2 inches (4,755 millimeters) in length.
Photo: Ministry of Industry and Information Technology China The upscaling of the 3 Series comes down to structural market differences. In the Chinese luxury car segment, many owners prefer to sit in the back seat, while a professional chauffeur handles the driving. That is why rear-seat legroom and rear-cabin premium features are highly appreciated.
BMW has ruled out bringing the long-wheelbase SUVs or sedans to the United States, as American buyers prefer cargo space along with the driver-focused experience and the high driving position. That is why the best-selling BMWs in the United States are the X3 and the X5.
It’s not just the wheelbase that sets the Chinese 3 Series apart. It rolls off the production line with modifications required by the local regulatory landscape. The car features semi-hidden door handles instead of the completely flush, retractable door handles seen elsewhere in the world.
This design shift is a response to safety regulations banning fully hidden door handles due to emergency extraction risks, following crashes involving other models in which occupants were trapped inside.
Photo: Ministry of Industry and Information Technology China The ICE-powered Chinese BMWs retain the modular CLAR architecture. The BMW 3 Series 325L and 330L come with the 2.0-liter turbocharged four-cylinder B48 engine, which produces 283 horsepower in top form and 231 horsepower for the base 325L. In the meantime, the i3 will sit on the Neue Klasse platform.
BMW has yet to disclose prices for the model that is expected to hit the Chinese market in 2027, CarNewsChina reports . However, customers should expect a price bump for the new generation.
The outgoing 3 Series starts at 258,000 yuan in China, which translates to roughly $36,000. In the meantime, the all-new U.S. model with the standard wheelbase is a $49,950 deal to begin with in the United States.

Bone Stock Original 1967 Pontiac GTO: One Owner Since New, Interior Is Flawless
44 photos
Photo: eBay seller primitivelandt
Original cars are the best cars, and this 1967 Pontiac GTO is here to prove it to everybody. The car is in fantastic shape for its age, especially considering that it has never been restored. It’s a babied GTO, and the more you inspect it, the more obvious it becomes that the car really can’t be cheap.
This isn’t something you see every day, and the seller explains the reason: this GTO spent its entire life with the same person who took it from the dealership.
It doesn’t mean it has barely been driven. Not at all, and the odometer is living proof, as it shows no more, no less than 101,000 miles. This is the original mileage, but considering this GTO never received a complete restoration, its condition is even more impressive.
How on Earth has someone managed to add 100K miles to this GTO without even leaving the print of their behind on their driver’s seat? That’s beyond me.
Photo: eBay seller primitivelandt The ultimate driving machine. This is how Pontiac described the GTO in its 1967 press papers, telling potential buyers that once they get this car, they “learn how beautiful life can really be.”
The GTO wasn’t significantly redesigned from the previous year, as Pontiac’s car drawing power was almost exclusively directed at its big cars. The taillights indeed received a refresh, and so did the grille, but the GTO wasn’t necessarily a new car from a design perspective.
What turned it into a completely new car was the army of engines under the hood.
The GTO was no longer offered with 389ci engines. Pontiac stroked the 389 to 400 cubic inches to obtain the engines that continued to be part of its lineup for one decade.
The base engine was a 400ci unit with a four-barrel carburetor. It produced 335 horsepower and ended up becoming the preferred choice for most GTO buyers. It delivered enough performance without having to spend more dollars.
Pontiac was aware that not everybody wanted a GTO for the power under the hood, so it also offered a de-tuned version of this unit. This time, the GM brand used a two-barrel carburetor, and the outcome was 255 horsepower.
Photo: eBay seller primitivelandt It didn’t stop here, though. Pontiac also wanted the GTO to deliver that boost of adrenaline that drivers loved, so the 400 could also be ordered in two high-performance configurations. Both developed 360 horsepower.
It worked. The GTO continued to be a very intriguing model, and most buyers ignored the two-barrel setup for obvious reasons. Pontiac ended the year with 81,722 GTOs shipped to American buyers.
This genuine 242 specimen was one of them. It was born with the standard 335-horsepower engine and a TH400 3-speed automatic transmission. This is the original setup, and it’s still in the car.
Photo: eBay seller primitivelandt The seller claims this GTO spent more than 20 years in storage, but contrary to what you’d normally expect, time hasn’t taken its toll on it. This is because the owner continued to baby the car, starting the engine regularly.
This is why the GTO is now prepared for the road, so if you want to take it for a spin to convince your significant other that it’s worth the money, you should be able to do this during an in-person inspection.
The Gulf Turquoise paint still looks good, but the seller is honest and reveals the obvious. The car is 99% rust-free, and there are signs of minor body repairs, such as the rear panel between the taillights and the passenger side. There are also small dings and bubbles, but these make sense, considering the car has never been refreshed completely.
The chrome looks good, and the trunk looks spotless after it received a rust-proofing treatment. The coated area is still gray, so it wasn’t painted, and the seller claims they made this decision for visual clarity.
Photo: eBay seller primitivelandt The GTO comes with sought-after options, such as a dash-mounted clock, a push-button radio, and a passenger vanity mirror on the visor. But there are also rare goodies.
“The car was ordered with bucket seats and an automatic shift selector on the column with no center console, which has proved to be somewhat rare,” the seller notes.
All of these make this GTO a fantastic restoration candidate, and there’s a good chance someone with the right skills will get it. But the right skills aren’t enough to get your hands on this car, as you also need the right money in your account.
The battle for the GTO is already underway, with the top offer now at $9,600. Unsurprisingly, the reserve is still in place, so the car won’t go anywhere unless someone comes up with a higher offer. The auction is scheduled to end in 8 days.
If you want to see the car in person, which I think is the best idea, considering you must double-check that everything is as advertised, you need to pack your bags for a trip to Elbert, California.

source_document.body:
PARIS — An industry consortium developing a European hypersonic interceptor plans to fly a full-systems demonstrator by the end of 2029, project leader MBDA said in a briefing at the Euronaval maritime-defense exhibition.
The program, named Hydis , is competing with the Hydef program coordinated by Spain’s Sistemas de Misiles to secure €100 million (US$112 million) in European funding for the second development phase of the interceptor. A decision about who will get the financing is due at the end of the month, Lionel Mazenq, MBDA’s vice president for program incubators, said Nov. 4.
While China and Russia have been developing hypersonic glide vehicles for attack, Europe lacks capabilities to intercept them, something Hydis and Hydef seek to address. Both projects received European funding for their initial development, but the European Defence Funds plans to fund only one of the two proposals as part of its 2026 work program.
The Hydis interceptor is designed to address a large number of threats that are “very diverse in terms of behavior,” Mazenq said. “Today nothing is able to intercept this portfolio of threats, absolutely nothing.”
With the final concept selected , the consortium is now undertaking a number of on-the-ground demonstrations to bring technology readiness to level 3 or 4 as part of the first phase of the project, the executive said. The commonly used technology readiness scale spans nine tiers, with the highest level representing a system completely developed and proven to work.
For the second phase, Hydis will expand to 36 industrial and research partners as well as 14 subcontractors, from the current 19 companies involved in the project, according to Mazenq. Companies joining the consortium include Safran, which will provide terminal-guidance sensors, as well as Thales, Saab and Leonardo for capabilities such as communication and data links.
The current three-year phase of Hydis, which runs until May 2027, has received €80 million in European funding, with additional funding of €57 million from the four supporting countries France, Italy, Germany and the Netherlands.
The project will expand to 17 countries for the second phase, with 11 member states contributing a combined €133 million of funding in addition to the European money, MBDA said. Germany is dropping out as a partner country for the second phase of the project, according to the briefing documents.
The companies involved in the project will also provide more than €10 million in combined funding, Mazenq said. The consortium is “working on fallback options” should the European Commission choose Hydef instead, though Mazenq said “we are thinking that we will win.”
The second phase is set to run from mid-2027 to mid-2029, and will include full-scale flight trials, according to Mazenq. At the end of the second phase, Hydis aims for a level of technology readiness between 3 and 6 for all functions, with a full-systems demonstrator “by the end of the decade, so very soon after.”
Production of the interceptor is scheduled to start in the first half of the 2030s, the executive said.
France, Italy, Belgium, the Netherlands, Sweden and Poland will provide “massive contributions” to the project, with smaller contributions from other countries, he said.
The MBDA executive presented a design for a four-stage missile, a “multi-stage stratospheric hypersonic interceptor” capable of dealing both with hypersonic threats arriving horizontally at medium altitudes, as well as ballistic missiles that approach with a relatively steep dive, and which must be intercepted “relatively early” in the upper layers of the atmosphere.
The Hydis partner countries as well as the European Commission requested an interceptor that covers both ballistic and hypersonic defense, “which requires, effectively, an additional effort in terms of design,” but brings advantages in terms of being able to stockpile a single missile against multiple threats, Mazenq said.
China is probably the country that is ahead in developing hypersonic weapons, more than Russia, with its DF-17 hypersonic glide vehicle the most advanced in service today, according to Mazenq.
“So being obsessed just by Russia is not the solution to prepare a robust system for defending Europe, not only the European continent, but also our forces deployed around the world,” the executive said.
The big challenge of intercepting hypersonic glide vehicles is their maneuverability at altitudes between 30 and 45 kilometers, which means that a slight turn can change the projected interception point by tens or hundreds of kilometers, according to the MBDA executive.
Predicting the trajectory of hypersonic threats will be key to intercepting them, with artificial intelligence running real-time models as soon as a target is detected to identify the right time and place to intercept, updated throughout the flight of the interceptor as it climbs towards its target, Mazenq said.
“This capability is absolutely essential because if you don’t have it, the pressure on the design of the interceptor is such that it’s impossible to do.”
Target and interceptor encounter velocity can reach 5 kilometers per second, according to Mazenq.
The only equivalent to the European program is the U.S. Glide Phase Interceptor project, which was awarded to Northrop Grumman, Mazenq said. The difference with the European project is that GPI only addresses the hypersonic glider threat, with intermediate-range ballistic missiles handled by exoatmospheric interceptors such as SM-3, according to the MBDA executive.
Hydis is aiming for a “robust design” that can be effective with a limited number of sensors. While the system is designed to be integrated with European space-based missile early-warning capabilities JEWEL and Odin’s Eye, it must also be capable of delivering “a good performance” with only a long-range radar, Mazenq said.
“That’s an additional challenge, but this is absolutely necessary to strengthen the future capability and to make it robust to all the conditions that can be encountered during a conflict.”
Hydis aims for its interceptor to cost less than a third of the unit price of an SM-3 missile, according to Mazenq, who didn’t clarify which version of the U.S. missile when asked. The SM-3 Block 1B missile costs $9.7 million to $12.5 million per intercept, while the price tag for the Block IIA missile is $27.9 million, according to the non-profit Missile Defense Advocacy Alliance.
The Hydis concept is hit-to-kill, and the interceptor builds on technology from existing programs, particularly MBDA’s Aster air-defense missile for flight control, while Italy’s Avio provides high-performance solid rocket motors. The system is designed to defeat a hypersonic threat with a maximum of two interceptors fired, according to Mazenq.
A visual comparison with the Aster B1 NT air-defense missile in the presentation indicated an interceptor that stands around 30% taller, with a length of about 7 meters (23 ft). Mazenq said the missile will be compatible with vertical-launch systems onboard ships, including the Mark 41 vertical-launch cell as well as a future version of Naval Group’s Sylver VLS.
“It’s effectively four-stage with a very high capability of acceleration, because we want to fire it as late as possible, due to the indetermination of the hypersonic threat trajectory,” Mazenq said. “So it’s a bit fat, but it’s a Formula 1. It’s hypersonic, truly hypersonic, not just Mach 5.”

Land Rover Welcomes Range Rover Sport Battersea Edition, Inspired by London But Sent to Australia
18 photos
Photo: Land Rover
According to the latest reports, corroborated by official quotes from the JLR corner office head honchos, Range Rover is going even more premium than before, a recent Autocar piece quotes Martin Limpert, the managing director of Range Rover, saying the fates of the Evoque and Velar are now sealed .
That means the cheaper models will retire to make it easy for customers to identify the positions of the Defender and Discovery, but reading between the lines, it’s pretty easy to understand that Jaguar Land Rover has decided that affordable SUVs aren’t worth the effort, instead moving Range Rover even more upmarket with the arrival of the recent Range Rover and Range Rover Sport Electric variants plus the upcoming Range Rover GT with both EV and hybrid power.
Until then, JLR continues to ‘print money’ with Range Rover via special editions: in Australia, they are now announcing the impending arrival of the Range Rover Sport Battersea Edition model. If the name sounds familiar, it’s because the SUV “presents a confident, contemporary interpretation of modern luxury, inspired by the architectural reinvention of London’s Battersea district.”
But there’s a second reason: back in April 2026, Land Rover announced no less than four special editions of Range Rovers aimed at taking the capital city of London to the road. Those were the Range Rover Evoque Hoxton Edition, the Range Rover Velar Belgravia Edition, the Range Rover Sport Battersea Edition , as well as the Range Rover Westminster Edition. They each honored a historic London neighborhood with a collection of special details, of course.
Now, the Range Rover Sport Battersea Edition is coming to the Land Down Under , and of course, it won’t be cheap: pricing in Australia kicks off at AU $179,990 driveaway, which is more than $126k at the current exchange rate. For the sum, Land Rover fans in general and Range Rover Sport enthusiasts in particular get the SUV dressed in Firenze Red, Fuji White, or Santorini Black, complete with a raft of enhancements.
Those include privacy glass, black brake calipers, Soft Door Close and a sliding panoramic roof, 20-way heated and ventilated memory front seats with heated power-recline rear seats. There’s also a Cold Climate Convenience Pack to add a heated steering wheel, heated windscreen and heated washer jets, along with a standard Meridian 3D Surround Sound System.
Specific to the Range Rover Sport Battersea Edition are the Pimento Red contrast stitching and matching seatbelts, Natural Black veneer with Battersea Edition script, specific treadplates and center console badging. The Battersea Edition features WiFi with data plan capability and the Technology Pack, the latter including a ClearSight interior rearview mirror, Head-Up Display, domestic plug socket and Park Assist, among other things.
“The Range Rover Sport Battersea Edition stands as a confident expression of contemporary luxury, a vehicle that blends heritage, performance and design into a singular, unmistakable statement,” said Tom Anderson, Head of Range Rover, Australia.

source_document.body:
Photo: BLUETTI
What do you actually need to keep running when the power goes out? For most households, the fridge, wifi, phones, and a few other essentials come first. Buying enough battery storage for every appliance in the house can come later – and that’s the appeal of BLUETTI’s latest launch, the Apex 200 portable power station .
The Apex 200 starts with 2.56kWh of storage and 3.2kW of continuous AC output, with the option to add batteries when you need longer backup. Built-in RV connections also mean it can earn its keep between blackouts.
BLUETTI launches the Apex 200 on November 4, with standalone super early-bird pricing starting at $1,099 through November 18 . Electrek readers can get an extra 5% off with code ELECTREK5OFF .
Here’s how to work out which setup is worth buying for your home or RV.
Advertisement - scroll for more content
Start with the battery you need now
Photo: BLUETTI
The Apex 200 takes the expandable design of BLUETTI’s flagship Apex series and puts it in a smaller package.
You get a 2,560Wh lithium iron phosphate (LFP) battery. The 3.2kW of continuous AC output increases to 3.6kW when an expansion battery is connected or the unit is actively charging.
The enclosure holds all that in 36.2 liters and weighs 26.9kg (59.3 lb). You’ll want two hands to move it, but it’s convenient to move it between home and your camper.
BLUETTI’s UltraCell technology delivers an industry-leading energy density of 70.7 Wh/L, yet the Apex 200 is more than 50% smaller by volume than class competitors. For an RV owner, that smaller footprint frees up room for other gear.
There’s also a tilted display and four app-controllable AC outlets. That might not sound like a big deal, but when the battery is on the floor or under your desk and you want to check or redirect its charge, it means you don’t have to crouch.
BLUETTI calls its approach “Start Small. Scale Big. Power More.” BLUETTI says Apex 300 users reported liking the modular design but wanted something easier to handle day to day. The Apex 200 offers them a lower entry point, with room to add capacity rather than replace the main unit.
How much battery do you need during a blackout?
Before buying a portable power station , you’ll want to know how much power your appliances draw and how much energy they use over time.
For example, a 150W appliance running continuously for 10 hours uses 1,500Wh. A 1,500W appliance gets through that same amount in one hour. Running a coffee maker briefly is a different proposition from keeping a high-draw appliance on all afternoon.
A rough runtime calculation is: Usable battery capacity in watt-hours ÷ average load in watts = hours of operation.
Divide the Apex 200’s nominal 2,560Wh by a steady 150W load, and you get about 17 hours before accounting for conversion losses and the battery system’s own power use. Real runtime will be lower.
Refrigerators complicate that calculation because their compressors cycle on and off. Check measured daily energy use where possible, along with startup demand – motors can briefly draw more power when they kick on.
For a short outage, the standalone unit is a sensible start
If your usual blackout lasts four to 12 hours, start by looking at the Apex 200 on its own.
BLUETTI estimates it can run a 150W refrigerator for 10–12 hours, or support low-draw essentials such as CPAPs, wifi routers, and mobile devices for two to three days, depending on the equipment and how it’s used. That doesn’t mean every device on that list will run together for three days. Your combined load determines the runtime.
The Apex 200 also gives you more control over where that energy goes. Four independently controllable Smart AC outlets built right into the unit – no need to buy smart plugs! – let you switch individual devices on and off through the BLUETTI App, set schedules, and apply state-of-charge controls. So if something doesn’t need power overnight, you can turn off its power at the outlet and save the fridge’s battery.
BLUETTI calls the feature an industry first for portable power stations. The system also works with Amazon Alexa, Google Home, and Home Assistant.
A UPS function switches connected equipment to battery power in 15 milliseconds. Check that switching time against your equipment’s requirements, especially for a CPAP or other sensitive device.
With AC output on and the display off, idle consumption drops to just 10.5W.
For a multi-day outage, add batteries – and plan for recharging
BLUETTI Apex 200 + 350W portable solar panel. Photo: BLUETTI
A winter freeze or severe storm can leave you without grid power for days. That’s when adding extra storage starts to make more sense.
For typical power outages, adding one or two BLUETTI B300K batteries can extend essential home backup to two to three days.
But you can go further. One Apex 200 supports up to six B500K expansion batteries, bringing its maximum capacity to 33.28kWh.
But a bigger battery still needs recharging eventually. The Apex 200 accepts up to 3kW of solar input across two independent channels:
A 2kW high-voltage MC4 input with a 60V–280V MPPT range.
A separate 1kW low-voltage XT60 input.
With a correctly configured array of SORA 500 portable solar panels making full use of those inputs, BLUETTI says the base battery can charge from 0 to 80% in 50 minutes, or reach 100% in 1.7 hours using solar alone.
A solar generator setup lets you recharge during daylight. The Apex 200 can also be charged with wall AC, vehicle charging, and compatible gas-generator charging. A suitable 30A generator connection can help replenish the battery when solar production falls short.
For broader home backup, check the complete configuration
The Apex 200 can also form part of a larger home battery backup system through BLUETTI’s Hub A1 parallel box.
BLUETTI specifies up to 6kW of continuous AC output and approximately 100kWh of storage across a parallel system using up to three Apex 200 units.
That’s a significant increase over the standalone battery, but your daily consumption still matters. A steady 1kW load uses 24kWh in 24 hours. Heavy-draw appliances can make a large battery feel much smaller.
BLUETTI positions its larger configurations for three to four days of essential-panel backup. How close you get depends on your batteries, appliances, and ability to recharge.
If you want automatic backup through your home’s electrical panel, confirm the compatible transfer equipment, supported circuits, voltage, and output for the exact bundle. Those details determine what you can actually keep running.
Which Apex 200 home bundle should you choose?
SORA 500 foldable solar panel. Photo: BLUETTI
Start with your most likely outage, then decide whether you need more runtime, a charging source, or both.
What you need | Suggested setup | Why it makes sense
Backup for a short blackout | Apex 200 standalone | Covers priority plug-in loads without buying expansion batteries upfront
Solar charging at home or off-grid | Apex 200 + SORA 500 solar panel | Adds daylight recharging, with room to build a larger compatible solar array
More runtime for family essentials | Apex 200 + one or two B300K batteries | Extends essential home backup to two to three days
A larger home backup setup | Up to three Apex 200s via HUB A1 | Delivers 6kW continuous AC output and around 100kWh total capacity for whole-home backup
Extra batteries extend runtime. Solar panels or another charging source recharge them. For outages that stretch into days, both can be worth having.
Road trip? The built-in ports matter
Photo: BLUETTI
When shopping for a camper van or travel trailer, choosing a battery comes down to more than just capacity. Among its 10 output ports are two connections RV owners will appreciate having built in.
The native 30A TT-30R RV outlet plugs directly into travel trailer shore power inlets for 120V power.
The 12V/30A Anderson port can directly power compatible DC equipment, including portable fridges and communications gear. This avoids converting battery power to AC and then back to DC, cutting out unnecessary conversion steps.
For charging between campsites, the system can pair with the BLUETTI Charger 2, which combines alternator and solar charging support. It lets you use driving time to replenish the battery through faster vehicle alternator charging, then use solar when you’re parked.
BLUETTI’s recommended mobile bundle is the Apex 200 + SORA 500 solar panel + Charger 2 . You get storage for camp, solar charging during your stay, and alternator charging on the road. Compatible campground AC gives you another option.
Should you buy the BLUETTI Apex 200 or Apex 300?
The Apex 200 is the better fit if you value a smaller enclosure, easier transport, native RV ports, and a lower upfront cost. You can start with 2.56kWh and expand to 33.28kWh on one unit, or approximately 100kWh across a fully expanded parallel system.
The Apex 300 is worth considering if your priority is higher native output and capacity for a system that will mostly stay at home. It offers 3,840W of output and 2,764.8Wh of battery storage , and BLUETTI positions it for more advanced home backup, including compatible 120V/240V configurations.

To build on the momentum in MASH, we—at Madrigal Pharmaceuticals and the industry more widely—must further expand approaches to diagnosis, monitoring and individualized treatment to help more patients.
For decades, metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis was one of the most challenging areas in drug development. Despite increasing scientific understanding and substantial investment across academia and industry, effective therapies remained elusive.
That changed in 2024 with the field’s first approved medicine , developed and commercialized by Madrigal Pharmaceuticals, where I serve as chief medical officer.
The impact of a first treatment often extends far beyond the medicine itself. It demonstrates that therapeutic intervention is possible and opens the door to a new phase of scientific and clinical discovery.
In diseases ranging from cystic fibrosis to chronic myeloid leukemia, breakthrough therapies have transformed not only treatment options, but also how patients are identified, monitored and studied. New diagnostics, care pathways and endpoints emerge. Treatment expectations shift, and subsequent innovations build upon the original breakthrough.
Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH) is now entering this exciting phase of renewed innovation.
A new era for liver health
MASH is a serious liver disease that is estimated to affect approximately 5% of adults in the United States, with consequences that extend beyond this critical organ. As understanding of the disease continues to grow, researchers are gaining greater insight into the connections between MASH and other aspects of cardiometabolic health, including obesity, type 2 diabetes and cardiovascular disease. For example, MASH has been identified as an independent risk factor for cardiovascular disease, and conversely, cardiovascular disease is the leading cause of mortality among patients with MASH.
This growing understanding is reshaping how researchers think about MASH biology and the therapeutic approaches needed to address it. Instead of looking at MASH through the lens of a single biological pathway, researchers are pursuing approaches that target different drivers of the disease, from the manifestations of metabolic dysfunction and dysregulated energy balance to inflammation, fibrosis and lipid handling.
MASH
Beyond Rezdiffra: The 4 Most Promising MASH Pipelines in Play
After last year’s ‘stampede’ for FGF21 assets, the focus for the metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis space has shifted toward differentiated approaches, such as THR-β agonists and combination treatments, that seek to mirror the commercial success of Madrigal’s Rezdiffra.
February 23, 2026
·
6 min read
·
Ben Hargreaves
Read more
Potential interventions include incretin-based therapies, FGF21-based approaches and DGAT2 inhibition, among other emerging mechanisms . Like many complex, multifactorial diseases, optimal treatment of MASH will likely involve multiple complementary mechanisms of action. Researchers are also identifying genetic factors that increase the risk of MASH progression, such as mutations in the PNPLA3 gene .
Together, these approaches may reflect a more complete understanding of how liver disease both influences and is influenced by broader cardiometabolic health—and highlight a growing interest in liver health’s effects on other outcomes throughout the body. The expanding range of mechanisms under investigation, along with growing investment across the industry, reflects increasing confidence in the future of MASH drug development.
That confidence is likely to accelerate the pace of innovation. In oncology, cardiovascular disease and diabetes, deeper insights into disease biology have ultimately led to multiple therapeutic classes, combination strategies and increasingly personalized approaches to care. MASH will similarly benefit from continued advances in understanding the disease’s complex biology, further expanding treatment options and supporting more individualized approaches.
Evolving diagnostics and monitoring of MASH
Realizing the full potential of MASH interventions will also depend on identifying and monitoring patients earlier and more effectively. Historically, MASH assessment has relied heavily on liver biopsy to assess disease severity. Advances in noninvasive tests are creating opportunities to assess liver fat and stiffness and other biomarkers of disease activity in a more patient-friendly manner.
This opportunity is particularly important given the substantial gap between the number of people living with MASH and those who have been diagnosed—only about 10% of patients are currently under the care of a specialist who treats the disease. As diagnostic capabilities improve, clinicians may be able to identify patients earlier, monitor treatment response more routinely and intervene before serious liver damage occurs.
The next chapter of MASH will be built on what the first approval makes possible: complementary therapeutic strategies and combinations, genetically targeted approaches informed by disease biology and better tools to identify and monitor patients and run more efficient trials.
The question facing the field is no longer whether progress can be made. It is how far that progress can take us.

Stellantis Uses Direct Connection to Unleash No Less Than Six New HEMI V8 Crate Engine Packages
8 photos
Photo: Stellantis
The 2026 SEMA Show and EICMA (aka the Esposizione Internazionale Ciclo Motociclo e Accessori or the International Exhibition of Cycles, Motorcycles, and Accessories) are continents apart - and that's actually a good thing. Imagine if you had to choose from either…
If you’re a fan of both four and two wheels (I’m developing a love for the latter myself), you’ll know that both the Las Vegas, Nevada gathering and the Milan, Italy trade fair are like Christmas coming early for custom rides and the latest and greatest bikes. But thanks to the power of the Internet, jumping back and forth between them is a trifle, unlike a flight which takes more than 14 hours.
So, you can check out the latest Yamaha scooter, the NMAX E all-electric model one moment and then skip to a roaring V8 courtesy of Stellantis the next. The US automaker has been pretty busy in and around the 2026 SEMA Show in Las Vegas, announcing at home in Auburn Hills the new Sub-Zero exterior color for the best-selling Dodge Durango three-row SUV , the SRT Performance Jeep Wrangler Scrambler Concept , or a new series of HEMI V8 crate engine packages through Direct Connection.
The latter novelty is a new program that combines the iconic V8, engine controller integration, and a three-year / 100,000-mile warranty for “complete turnkey packages geared toward both manual and automatic transmission applications.” The all-new Direct Connection crate engine packages with controller kit offer horsepower ratings from ‘just’ 385 hp to no less than 1,025 horsepower with flex fuel capability.
All of them will have new and exclusive-branded shipping crates to “celebrate the heritage and performance legacy of SRT and Direct Connection”; availability starts in the first quarter of 2027 and final pricing will be announced at a later date. Direct Connection, the official factory-backed performance parts arm of Stellantis’ SRT Performance division, announced the all-new series of crate engine packages at the 2026 SEMA Show complete with serialized engine identification plaques.
The six new packages consist of the 345 Crate HEMI Street Strip with 385 hp and 417 lb-ft torque, recommended for the TorqueFlite 8HP90 automatic transmission kit or the Tremec Magnum manual application; the 345 Crate HEMI Super Stock; the 392 Crate HEMI Street Strip or Super Stock with 485 horsepower and 475 lb-ft torque (manual and auto both); and the Hellcrate Redeye 6.2L Supercharged Crate HEMI Super Stock with up to 885 hp and 787 lb-ft of torque in High Octane Mode or the Hellephant C170 Super Stock with up to 1,025 horsepower and 945 lb-ft torque on E85 blend.
The Direct Connection display also features the restored 1967 Plymouth GTX, first shown at SEMA in 2024 and it returned to be equipped with the newly announced Hellcrate Redeye 6.2 crate engine package. “When we showed this GTX at SEMA in 2024, the original owner we bought it from wasn’t exactly thrilled that we had turned his muscle car into an EV,” said Tim Kuniskis. We heard him. So, this year, we fixed it. We put a supercharged HEMI back under the hood, and I have a feeling he’s going to like this version a whole lot better.”

Volkswagen Commercial Vehicles Relaunches the Caravelle Nameplate In the UK, Starting From £41,960*
6 photos
Photo: Volkswagen Commercial Vehicles
Volkswagen Commercial Vehicles may be dedicated solely to VW AG’s light commercial vehicles, but it’s entirely committed to its job, like all professionals are. So, it’s no wonder that they often have more news up and coming than some larger mainstream brands.
Just recently, they said they were busy making various announcements in the United Kingdom: VCV has been named the ‘Most Reliable Vanmaker’ for the third consecutive year by the UK’s fleet companies in the Fleet News FN50 annual rankings, but they also have product novelties.
In addition to the showcase of the flexible autonomous ID. Buzz platform at NVIDIA GTC Berlin, back in October Volkswagen Commercial Vehicles kicked off the preparations for the 2027 camping season with the Grand California campervan getting updates for MY27, like a new interior and optional solar panels, while a Dune Special Edition was also added to the UK lineup.
That’s not all, because just a few days ago the UK order books were opened for the facelifted California campervan , with first deliveries expected in early 2027 and prices kicking off at £54,065 or $73k, with the refreshed models featuring an improved front-end design, updated cockpit, and the latest comfort and safety technologies, with added benefits like the 5+ Promise, Volkswagen’s enhanced warranty and service plan.
Anyway, they are not slowing down, and now Volkswagen Commercial Vehicles is replacing the outgoing Multivan moniker with a fresher premium seven-seat people carrier as the brand reintroduces the Caravelle nameplate to the UK. Available to order starting November 5, 2026, it is priced from £41,960 or about $53,539 at the current exchange rate.
However, there’s a caveat: just like in the case of the refreshed California campervan, the new Caravelle is priced without VAT, so you're going to have to pay more if you can't deduct the tax in the UK . Anyway, the new seven-seat people carrier can also be had from £499 per month on a Solutions Personal Contract Plan, with first customer deliveries expected in early 2027.
It has a new exterior and interior style, the latest technology, seven seats as standard, as well as an optional six-seat configuration. It will be available with the regular Life and Style trims but also with a new Edition grade starting from £49,960 (excl. VAT), which is over $63k. There are features like the new VW Bus headlights, a new-generation ‘free-standing’ 12.9-inch infotainment system, as well as an upgraded 10.25-inch Digital Cockpit.
There are two solid colors, eight metallic paints, and even three dual-tone finishes (Candy White/Starlight Blue metallic, Candy White/Grey Brown Metallic, Grenadilla Black Metallic/Sunset Red Metallic), plus a Black Roof option exclusively for the Edition trim.
The latter brings a dark-tinted two-piece panoramic sunroof, glossy black 18-inch Brussel alloy wheels, and dark LED rear lights, plus dark silver brushed inserts; a dark headliner and door pillar trim; and ergoComfort seats in dark ArtVelours microfleece upholstery for the interior.

Biotech and pharma professionals share job hunt challenges after being let go, while a recruiting expert discusses why hiring managers prefer candidates without employment gaps and how to address gaps in interviews.
As the industry has grappled with issues including funding woes , patent expirations and tariff threats , layoffs have hit biopharma employees hard, based on a BioSpace LinkedIn poll. It found that 64% of respondents have been let go in the past five years, and just over 1 in 5 (22%) have lost their jobs at least twice.
For those who experience layoffs more than once, which can lead to multiple employment gaps , the impact on their careers can be significant. Several respondents to a BioSpace survey, all of whom have been let go twice in the past five years, touched on that challenge. One noted that their career has stopped. They had a senior role but now can’t find a full-time job and have turned to part-time consulting.
Another commented that repeated layoffs due to organizational restructures have disrupted their professional trajectory. They explained that being let go has created uncertainty and made it more challenging to maintain their career continuity and long-term professional growth, despite their experience and contributions.
Yet another wrote, “Many recruiters and hiring managers don’t want to bother with someone frequently let go.” Getting through HR screening and being taken seriously by the hiring manager is harder, they added.
In one case, however, being let go twice led to a positive outcome. A survey respondent shared that it gave them the push they needed to start two small businesses. Multiple participants in a BioSpace survey last year shared similar stories of becoming their own bosses as the upside of being laid off .
Why multiple layoffs make it harder to get hired
For those striving to move from laid off to employed, it can be a challenging endeavor. Bryan Blair, vice president of biotech and pharma recruiting at GQR Global Markets, told BioSpace that when all things are equal, his clients almost always choose candidates who have never been let go. While employers can be understanding about layoffs depending on the circumstances behind them, he said, being let go is generally viewed as a blemish on someone’s resume and is probably one of the most common reasons candidates are rejected.
When it comes to multiple layoffs, Blair noted that they can affect someone’s chances of getting hired “in an astronomical way.”
“If we all put ourselves in the shoes of a hiring manager, you’re going to be responsible for this person that you’re bringing in,” he said. “You’re going to have to answer to their performance. You’re going to have to get signoff on approving their offer and everything. That stuff becomes so much easier when you have a resume that you’re presenting that is a linear progression through job titles with no gaps of employment.”
That said, layoffs are not always evident on resumes. Blair noted that some biopharma professionals, especially those let go for the first time, will make it look like they’re still employed. Instead of listing an end date for their most recent company, he explained, they state “present.”
“The gamble pays off for them on most occasions,” Blair said. “It really kind of makes you think: Is the current way we evaluate these things super fair, because when somebody is doing something deceptive like that, it can work to their advantage.”
When considering resumes he receives for open positions, Blair estimated that the practice of using “present” for roles that ended in layoffs has increased probably five times in the past five years.
Addressing layoffs during interviews
Once biopharma professionals who have been let go multiple times are at an interview, Blair recommended against bringing up their job losses while also being prepared to talk about them if asked. One tip he shared is that if someone was part of a large-scale workforce reduction that involved public information about the cuts, such as a news report, they should make sure they communicate their layoff’s scope.
“It makes it clear that it has nothing to do with your performance,” he said.
If there isn’t public information on the layoff, Blair noted, things can get tricky. For example, a hiring manager may wonder if the person is saying they were let go, but they were actually fired, he said.
If a biopharma professional wasn’t part of a large-scale workforce reduction that made headlines, Blair advised they do their absolute best to explain the nature of their situation. If their former employer eliminated the entire pharmacovigilance department after a drug failed in a clinical trial, he noted, they should share that information.
After they explain the reason they were let go, Blair recommended biopharma professionals talk about the layoff being a valuable learning experience. They could share what they took away from it and how it made them recognize that they can’t take jobs for granted, he noted.
“I think that when you can bring those elements in and show that it was a positive for you, that’s going to be your best chance,” Blair said.

Google Really Wants You To Try Its New Google Maps Feature, So It'll Start Automatically in Airports
9 photos
Photo: Google
The Google Maps team is working on multiple fronts, so in addition to immersive navigation and the integration of Gemini , it’s also developing other features that might not be getting the love Google hoped. Ask Maps is one of these features, as a recently discovered feature currently in the works suggests that Google wants more people to use it.
Ask Maps debuted earlier this year as a way to turn the experience with Google Maps into a conversation that’ll help you use the app more efficiently, discover places, get information about certain locations, and configure navigation.
Ask Maps is more of an assistant integrated directly into Google Maps. Powered by artificial intelligence, this feature makes it much easier to find what you’re looking for without having to filter the results, search the web, or anything like that. Just ask maps.
Now, the thing that Google is reportedly working on is a feature that allows the Ask Maps experience to kick in automatically when you’re in an airport. Technically, Google Maps would use your location to figure out when you’ve just landed, assuming that you need help to explore a new city or region.
This is when Ask Maps would come in handy the most, as it would automatically kick in after you land specifically to help with this exploration mission.
Photo: Google Evidence found in the most recent version of Google Maps for Android indicates that Google has already added support for a long list of airports, meaning that these would be the places where Ask Maps would fire up automatically. When it appears on the screen, Ask Maps shows a message that includes a warm welcome and then offers to help with finding a “great first meal” and getting into town.
Theoretically, Ask Maps would become a guide for tourists, though the automatic launch indicates that Google wants to make sure people know this feature is there. There’s a chance Ask Maps isn’t getting the user attention Google initially hoped for, so this approach would make more people aware that a conversational-based experience is bundled with Google Maps.
Just like any other feature that is currently in the works, we’d better not hold our breath for this major update to land on our devices. It wouldn’t be the first time Google gives up on a new feature before it lands in the production channel, so let’s just wait and see what happens.
Photo: Google The immersive navigation update Meanwhile, there are other reasons to be excited about Google Maps updates.
The search giant is still rolling out the immersive navigation update to the first users, though it’s unclear when everybody else is supposed to get it.
Google described this Google Maps refresh as the biggest update in over a decade, as it includes more detailed maps, such as trees, crosswalks, and traffic lights. Google has also improved the navigation experience with see-through passes and more detailed guidance powered by Gemini.
Beginning with this update, Google Maps no longer offers just standard turn-by-turn directions, such as “turn right in one mile.” The application uses Gemini power to check the route and look for landmarks that can be used during navigation. This means you’ll be instructed to “turn right after the gas station” or to “continue straight and then turn right after the Apple store.”
The immersive navigation update has already started to roll out, but the availability continues to be very limited. It’s only live in the United States and Canada, and despite Google promising to bring it to more regions, including in Europe, the update involves substantial work that can’t be finalized overnight. Availability should improve next year, when the immersive update should also go live in more regions.
Photo: Google Google is also connecting Google Maps with Gemini. With Gemini Personal Intelligence, the application will be able to provide navigation information based on what the AI-powered assistant can find in other Google products, such as Gmail and Google Calendar.
Once Gemini is aware of the data in your inbox or your next appointments, the assistant can instruct Google Maps to configure routes to your destinations. For example, once you arrive at a new airport after the flight is completed, Google Maps can fire up the Ask Maps feature and offer to look for something to do until the next meeting saved in your calendar takes place.
The same for your inbox, as Gemini can look for places where you need to be and tell Google Maps to configure a route.
Google hasn’t yet announced the new Ask Maps experience, but considering all the improvements that the company is making on multiple fronts, including artificial intelligence and Gemini integration, focusing more on the conversational side of the navigation app makes sense. I wouldn’t hold my breath for an imminent rollout, though, as this feature is more likely to appear next year.

Waze Might Soon Start Warning Drivers About Cyclists on the Road Thanks to Garmin Watches
6 photos
Photo: Bogdan Popa/autoevolution
Waze might soon be getting a new alert, as Garmin, the famous maker of so many things, including smartwatches, GPS navigators , aviation and marine technology, is exploring a new way to make the road a safer place for cyclists.
Garmin wants Waze drivers to be alerted whenever they are about to come across a cyclist on the road, therefore reducing the likelihood of a crash.
It all starts with one of Garmin’s main focuses and the horrible statistics that land every year.
Garmin is investing high dollars in cycling and related technology, including smartwatch - which yes, also include bicycle tracking and statistics - and cycling computers with or without GPS. It’s also making additional devices, such as dual-sensing meter pedals, radars, and lights for bicycles.
Photo: Bogdan Popa/autoevolution Fatal crashes involving cyclists Unfortunately for both Garmin and everybody else, the number of fatalities involving cyclists is still at worrying levels. IIHS data shows that between 2022 and 2024, over 1,000 people were killed on the road. More worrying is that not all cyclists care about their safety on the road, and no more, no less than 68% of those who lost their lives following a crash in 2024 were not wearing helmets.
Most deaths - 858 - happened on city roads and 658 crashes took place in places without an intersection.
Enter Waze.
Garmin has the data Garmin has found a way to forward cyclist location data to the Google-owned traffic navigation app to make drivers aware that they might be coming across someone riding a bike. There’s a good reason why I said might , and I’ll elaborate in a minute.
Basically, Garmin already knows where every cyclist is located when they start tracking on one of the company’s devices (obviously, if the cyclists themselves allow this information to be shared).
LiveTrack, a built-in Garmin feature allows the device, most often a smartwatch, to keep tabs on the cyclist’s location and share with pre-defined contacts. These can be their wives, friends, kids, and so on, but the idea is that someone else can always know where you are when you are riding your bike.
Photo: Bogdan Popa/autoevolution That is why Garmin seemingly believes that the data can be used in a more efficient way. The most recent version of Garmin Connect 5.31 includes references to a feature that would allow LiveTrack data to be shared with Waze, presumably to highlight the location of the cyclist on the map for nearby drivers.
An APK teardown exposed references to a feature called “Waze Location Sharing.” The description of the feature is still vague, but reads that users can “share location with Waze” and “share rides with Waze.”
The big questions It’s still unclear how this is going to work, but there are still several big questions that are left without an answer at this point.
While the main benefit of this Garmin - Waze integration would be a feature to highlight the location of a cyclist on the map, there’s also a chance that the target is a less ambitious objective. Garmin could allow cyclists to share their location with Waze only to allow a Waze user to see it. This means that the location wouldn’t be highlighted on the map for every nearby driver but only for a selected contact.
Photo: Bogdan Popa/autoevolution If everybody on the road sees the cyclist's location, the big question is how this is going to work in terms of notifications shown on the screen. Cyclists are very common in some places, so getting alerts after alerts would eventually affect the experience with the navigation app. Something similar happened when Waze rolled out speed bump notifications , and on roads with more than just a handful of speed bumps, drivers were literally spammed with alerts.
If the location of a cyclist appears on the map without a notification, this means drivers need to look at the screen regularly. This would work similarly to other Waze features, such as the initial version of speed limit changes, when a speed limit indicator only appeared on the map.
There are also other questions related to how Garmin is going to offer this feature in the first place. While Garmin charges a premium for its device, it’s not a secret that the company wants to turn its subscription-based model into a money-making machine.
Photo: Bogdan Popa/autoevolution While Garmin Connect+ initially debuted as a service whose actual benefit was almost non-existent, with Garmin locking less appealing goodies, such as special monthly challenges, behind a subscription, the company could expand it to more features, such as this upcoming Waze integration.
For now, the feature is still in the works, and I wouldn’t hold my breath to see it going live anytime soon. Theoretically, Garmin still has enough time to bring it to users by the end of the year, but considering it’s winter almost everywhere worldwide, the company might be holding it back until the spring, when the number of cyclists on the road should increase significantly and such a feature would make more sense.
